text:
tess: Quick follow-up from the INC postmortem — proposing a tiny pager circuit-breaker + alert scoring change to cut down duplicate pages during short compaction flaps. Idea: hold duplicate pages for 2m per alert key, then escalate if it persists.

omar: Sounds good. Which alerts do you mean specifically?

tess: Primarily: 
- compactor-high-latency (owner: storage)
- compactor-retries (owner: storage)
- scheduler-rate-limit-exceeded (owner: infra)

Also a policy change: if the same host fires two of these within 5m, group them into a single page with combined context instead of 2 separate pages.

liam: Can we get away with a 90s dedupe window instead of 2m? Our median MTTR on these is ~3m but a 90s window might still help.

tess: 90s might be ok; I picked 2m to be conservative. We should pick values based on signal TTL and the observed burst patterns. Action: run a 7d histogram of inter-arrival times for these alerts. (owner: liam, due EOW).

anika: We should also make sure on-call routing doesn't escalate to SEV2 automatically on duplicate. Some duplicates are noise and adds churn. Proposal: only escalate on persistent or increasing error rate, not on simple repeats.

omar: +1 to that. Can we add an "escalation hold" flag that blocks auto-escalation for the first 5m unless error rate > X?

tess: Yes — sketching rules:
- dedupe window: 90s (adjust after analysis)
- host grouping window: 5m -> group alerts by host and aggregate counts
- escalation hold: 5m unless 95th percentile error rate > 10/min

Put into playbook with clear owners and timelines.

liam: I'll run the inter-arrival and burst analysis today and post results. If we see >60% of duplicates within 90s, I'll greenlight 90s. Otherwise bump to 2m. (owner: liam, due: 2026-03-30)

anika: I'll update the on-call routing policy doc to add the escalation hold option and examples for SEV1/SEV2. (owner: anika, due: 2026-04-02)

tess: I'll open the alert PR with suggested dedupe/grouping rules and add unit tests for grouping logic. Also need a monitoring check that verifies dedupe isn't hiding a real outage (safety net). (owner: tess, due: 2026-03-31)

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-03 follow-up checklist updated by tess — https://pd.example/incidents/INC-2026-03/followups

omar: One more: add a weekly sweep to look for recurring patterns (same host, same morning window). Could be cron spike or maintenance job. (owner: infra, rotation: weekly on-call)

liam: Noted — I'll produce the histogram + a short writeup and link PRs.

anika: I'll coordinate with platform-ops to ensure the grouping logic is on the non-critical path so we don't add latency to alerting.

tess: Summary of action items: 
- liam: inter-arrival burst analysis + writeup (due 2026-03-30)
- tess: alert PR + safety net checks (due 2026-03-31)
- anika: routing doc + escalation hold examples (due 2026-04-02)
- infra (weekly on-call): recurring pattern sweep (recurring)

If anyone wants to change owners or timelines, shout now. Otherwise I'll open the PRs and assign the tasks. :thumbsup:

omar: Fine by me. Thanks — will monitor next week's on-call for regressions.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder scheduled: follow-up review meeting 2026-04-06 16:00 UTC (30m).

tess: Added agenda: results from liam's histogram, PR diff, any regressions seen in week after rollout.

liam: I'll ping when analysis is done and post the CSV + small chart in this thread.

anika: Thanks all.
